subject: BrightWave: sustained p99 tail and routing policy - immediate mitigation plan

Subject: Re: API behaviour - sudden p99 increase (BrightWave)

Hi Logan,

We're seeing an ongoing p99 latency increase on our production traffic since ~02:00 PT. UX reports and a handful of failed checkouts correlate with time windows where requests appear queued for multiple seconds before tokens are produced. Our average token throughput hasn't changed from our end.

Summary:
- p50 ~= 200ms, p95 ~= 450ms, p99 jumps to 3.5–6s in ~10% of requests over last 6 hours
- Error-rate small (0.4%) but customer-facing timeouts are happening
- No config changes on our side; model pinned to redwood/gpt-l-1.3b:v2

We opened a ticket (BrightWave#1329) — attaching a sample trace and the request id list. Can you escalate? This is affecting a small cohort of checkout flows and we need an immediate mitigation while you investigate root cause.

Attaching: sample-trace-9.log, request-ids.txt

Thanks,
Anna

Hi Anna — thanks for the heads up and the trace. I've looped in Marcus (CS lead) and Laura (SRE) to triage immediately.

Immediate plan:
1) Marcus will pull server-side traces and confirm whether queueing/backpressure or model-side slowdown is the dominant signal.
2) If queueing/backpressure in our fronting layer, we can temporarily increase BrightWave's concurrency cap for the next 4 hours and route to a higher-throughput pool while we root cause.
3) I'll coordinate a short exec sync if we need credits/contract exceptions.

We treat this as high priority — I'll update in the next 30–60m.

— Logan

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API behaviour - sudden p99 increase (BrightWave)

Thanks Logan — looking at traces now. Initial findings:
- A subset of requests for BrightWave are hitting sustained queue lengths in the request-router for their tenant key.
- The kernel-level execution times for tokens are within expected bounds; CPU/GPU busy time doesn't spike correlating with p99 windows.
- KV cache hit-rate for their request patterns dropped to ~48% during incidents (baseline ~86%) — likely causing extra token compute for repeated prefixes.

I've uploaded a zipped set of p99 traces and the request id list to the shared drive. See: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Brw-Support-Traces (linked)
[Attachment: brightwave-p99-traces.zip (zip)]

Questions for SRE:
- Is the concurrency cap for WR-tenant BRW-839 still at the conservative default of 16? Can we do a safe bump to 32 for the next 4 hours and monitor backpressure metrics?
- Can we temporarily enable more aggressive KV cache retention for this tenant to bring hit-rate back up?

If both are feasible, that should reduce queueing-induced p99 while we dig into why cache hit-rate regressed.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: API behaviour - sudden p99 increase (BrightWave)

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 10:05 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> - Is the concurrency cap for WR-tenant BRW-839 still at the conservative default of 16? Can we do a safe bump to 32 for the next 4 hours and monitor backpressure metrics?
> - Can we temporarily enable more aggressive KV cache retention for this tenant to bring hit-rate back up?

I pulled the tenant config and infra metrics: the concurrency cap is indeed at 16. Allocation shows BRW-839 on the mixed-performance host pool (pool-mix-4), which is currently operating at ~72% aggregate utilization. We have headroom to move them to pool-highthroughput-2 or increase per-tenant concurrency.

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (non-disruptive):
- Increase concurrency cap from 16 -> 32 for BRW-839 for a 4-hour window (auto-revert)
- Enable tenant-specific KV cache retention policy: keep larger prefix cache for 30 minutes instead of 5, and bump cache size soft-limit by 25% for BRW-839
- Enable request-priority-exempt routing so queued BRW requests preferentially go to warmed hosts instead of being batched into long queues

Risk notes:
- Bumping concurrency increases host-side memory pressure; we'll watch OOM and swap trends.
- If we route to pool-highthroughput-2, costs increase (billback to account). If routing is required >12h, recommend a commercial exception or temporary credit.

I can push the changes at 13:45 PT once you confirm. Also attaching a snapshot of KV cache stats we took earlier.
[Attachment: kv-cache-snapshot.json (json)]

— Laura

Subject: Re: BrightWave: sustained p99 tail and routing policy - immediate mitigation plan

Hi Anna — quick update and next steps (TL;DR below).

What we saw and immediate fix applied: 
- Root symptom: tenant-level queueing causing long-tail latency; kernel token times normal.
- Actions executed at 13:50 PT: concurrency cap increased 16 -> 32 (auto-revert in 4h), KV cache retention increased, request-priority-exempt routing enabled. We also staged a failover route to pool-highthroughput-2 (not switched yet).
- Early results: p99 reduced from ~4.2s to ~800–1,200ms in the first 90m; KV hit-rate back to ~78%.

Ask of BrightWave:
- Could you confirm whether the affected checkout cohort used any unusual prompt prefixes or very long prefixes? That will help us validate whether KV patterns caused the regression.

Next steps (owners):
- Laura: monitor OOM/memory and host utilization; post 30m and 2h metric snapshots to the drive link. (owner: laura.bennett)
- Marcus: continue trace analysis and build an RCA outline (owner: marcus.lin)
- Logan: coordinate credit/contract conversation if we need >8h of routing (owner: logan.wright)
- Evelyn: internal exec aware and approved short window of mitigation; will decide on longer routing or credits if metrics don't fully normalize.

Attached: mitigation-playbook.pdf (steps taken and rollback guidance).
[Attachment: mitigation-playbook.pdf (pdf)]

We appreciate the quick signal — we'll continue to monitor closely and will follow up by tomorrow EOD with a draft RCA and customer note.

Best,
Logan
